subject.title: Support multiple gateway tokens for multi-user session isolation

question: Should OpenClaw core add a native Gateway principal/token model for per-user token identity and session isolation, or keep multi-user identity outside token mode for now?
rationale: This would add public auth/config semantics and change how Gateway credentials map to users, scopes, sessions, and auditability, so automation should not choose the boundary.

options.title: Sponsor a Gateway principal design
options.body: Keep this issue open as the per-user token/session-isolation design thread and require a scoped proposal that reconciles https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92367 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/68353 before code.

options.title: Keep multi-user identity in a front layer
options.body: Document the private-Gateway/front-layer pattern, including Pinchy-style deployments, and close or defer native per-token identity until a stronger core need appears.

options.title: Defer until scoped tokens land
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92367 settle bearer-scoped principals first, then revisit whether user labels and session isolation belong in the same token entries.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a Gateway principal design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the per-user token/session-isolation design thread and require a scoped proposal that reconciles https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92367 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/68353 before code.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current trusted-proxy identity-bearing auth mode and are the strongest history-backed owner for comparing token-mode identity against the existing proxy identity boundary.
